candidates.old:
LDY dm_index
    LDA arena_top_lo,X              \ the block starts at the arena's top: its header there,
    STA save_start_lo,Y             \ where parts 2 and 3 start (0: none)
    STA mark_part.header_lo
    SEC                             \ v_ptr = the start - 4: the first column's record goes at
    SBC #4                          \ v_ptr + 8, after the header (draw_column)
    STA v_ptr
    LDA arena_top_hi,X
    STA save_start_hi,Y
    STA mark_part.header_lo + 1
    SBC #0
    STA v_ptr + 1
    LDA v_ptr                       \ mark_part's base: the start - 8 (C = 1: the high byte did not borrow)
    SBC #4
    STA mark_part.base_lo
    LDA v_ptr + 1
    SBC #0
    STA mark_part.base_hi
    LDA arena_top_lo,X
    ADC #0                          \ C = 1 (no borrow above): the start + 1
    STA mark_part.header_hi
    LDA arena_top_hi,X
    ADC #0
    STA mark_part.header_hi + 1
    LDA #0
    LDY #7                          \ the header, at v_ptr + 4 to + 7
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY
candidates.new:
LDY dm_index
    LDA arena_top_hi,X              \ the high byte first, to everywhere it goes: the block's start, the start - 4,
    STA save_start_hi,Y             \ the start - 8 and the start + 1 share it unless the low byte borrows or
    STA mark_part.header_lo + 1     \ carries (room_fix, below, 9 starts in 256)
    STA v_ptr + 1
    STA mark_part.base_hi
    STA mark_part.header_hi + 1
    LDA arena_top_lo,X              \ the block starts at the arena's top: its header there,
    STA save_start_lo,Y             \ where parts 2 and 3 start (0: none)
    STA mark_part.header_lo
    INC A                           \ 65C02 opcode: the start + 1, low byte (&FF wraps to 0)
    STA mark_part.header_hi
    SEC                             \ A = the start - 8, low byte; C = 0 only if the start + 1 (low byte) is
    SBC #9                          \ under 9: the start's low byte &FF or under 8
    BCS room_ok
    CMP #&FC                        \ A = low - 8: &FC-&FF, the start's low byte &04-&07
    BCS room_base                   \ the start - 8 borrows from the high byte, the start - 4 does not
    CMP #&F8
    BCC room_carry                  \ A = &F7: low byte &FF, the start + 1 carries into the high byte
    DEC v_ptr + 1                   \ low byte &00-&03: the start - 4 borrows as well
.room_base
    DEC mark_part.base_hi
    BRA room_set                    \ 65C02 opcode
.room_carry
    INC mark_part.header_hi + 1
.room_set
    SEC
.room_ok
    STA mark_part.base_lo           \ mark_part's base: the start - 8 (C = 1)
    ADC #3                          \ the start - 4: v_ptr, the first column's record at v_ptr + 8 (draw_column)
    STA v_ptr
    LDA #0
    LDY #7                          \ the header, at v_ptr + 4 to + 7
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY
    STA (v_ptr),Y
    DEY
candidates.summary: put_on's .room: the start's high byte (the same for the start, start - 4, start - 8 and start + 1 unless the low byte borrows or carries, 9 starts in 256) is stored to all five places from one load, then the low byte makes start + 1 (INC A), start - 8 (one SEC/SBC #9 on start + 1, whose carry is also the test that no fix is needed) and start - 4 (ADC #3 on C = 1), with no reloads of v_ptr, v_ptr + 1 or the arena top. The rare starts (low byte &FF or &00-&07) take a fix block placed in the flow (BCS room_ok skips it) that DECs/INCs the high bytes already stored. 107 -> 90 cycles on the common path, 76 bytes for 72; the header-zeroing tail is unchanged (A = 0, Y = 4 at the end, as line 1382 needs).
candidates.equivalence: Outputs: save_start_lo/hi[Y], mark_part.header_lo/+1 (= start), header_hi/+1 (= start + 1), base_lo/hi (= start - 8), v_ptr/+1 (= start - 4), and the tail's A = 0, Y = 4, X unchanged (draw_mover's first act is LDX dm_slot). Checked for every low byte 0-255, every high byte 1-255 and either entry carry by a literal simulation of both sequences (identical results). Common path (low byte &08-&FE): A = low + 1 after INC A; SEC/SBC #9 gives A = low - 8 and C = 1 exactly when (low + 1) mod 256 >= 9; BCS room_ok taken; base_lo = low - 8; ADC #3 with C = 1 gives low - 4 = v_ptr's low byte; no borrow or carry reaches the high byte (low >= 8 so start - 4 and start - 8 do not borrow; low <= &FE so start + 1 does not carry), so the plain high byte stored to v_ptr + 1, base_hi and header_hi + 1 is right. Rare path (C = 0; A = low - 8 mod 256 = &F7 for low &FF, &F8-&FF for low 0-7): CMP #&FC / BCS room_base for low 4-7 (only start - 8 borrows: DEC base_hi); else CMP #&F8 / BCC room_carry for A = &F7 (low &FF: INC header_hi + 1, start - 4 and start - 8 do not borrow); else low 0-3 (start - 4 and start - 8 both borrow: DEC v_ptr + 1 and DEC base_hi). Every rare exit does SEC and falls into room_ok with A still = low - 8, so STA base_lo / ADC #3 / STA v_ptr give the same low bytes. The original's own assumption (C = 1 after the high-byte SBC #0, i.e. the arena's high byte >= 1; it is &30-&3F) is the one the new code needs (DEC of a stored high byte >= 1). A passlock of the change (scratch copy, control = HEAD build, seed 1, 2,500 passes, --screen --unclobber): state and screen identical every pass. The changed order of the stores (v_ptr + 1 before v_ptr, the operands before the low bytes) is invisible: nothing in an interrupt reads v_ptr (&C4/&C5), save_start_* or mark_part's operands, and mark_part is not run between the window's first and last store.
candidates.relies_on: Entry: X = back as in the original; A, Y and the flags dead on entry (the original loads Y first and sets C itself). Exit: A = 0, Y = 4 for line 1382's STA (v_ptr),Y; X unchanged; flags dead (draw_mover starts LDX dm_slot). The arena's high byte >= 1 (main RAM &3xxx). No label of the window is referenced from outside (.room is above the window; room_ok, room_base, room_carry, room_set are new and unique to this candidate; mark_part's operands are only written here and in put_on's tail). Page crossings (unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, scratch copy, Baron 0.5.3, pcprof seed 1, 1,500 passes, 2026-10-22): the window grows 4 bytes (72 -> 76), so everything after it in bank 4 slides up 4 (mark_part, draw_mover, the rest of the renderer); BCS room_ok is &99DB -> &99F0, same page (3 cycles); no branch in the window crosses a page. The slide moved under 2 cycles between 256-byte chunks, net about zero: render 23,430 -> 23,406 a pass, work a pass -24 (the window 172.5 -> 146.9; the shortfall against the claim is the rare path, about 3.5% of puts, and the slide). Same game (79,922 cycles a pass in total). The RIGHT-held game and the shift builds were not run; the gate does.
